messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Luca Moretti <luca.moretti@novabanc.com>, Sofia Patel <sofia.patel@novabanc.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Cross-border access & hosting model assessment — NovaBanc follow-up

Hi Luca / Sofia —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to understand the scope. Quick recap and the items we need to qualify so we can recommend the right hosting path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on‑prem):

Key constraints we heard
- EU customers' transaction data must be stored and processed within EU jurisdictions (GDPR + internal policy).
- APAC pilot will run SaaS-forward; lower residency requirements but latency target ~120–150ms for APAC endpoints.
- Internal US reporting services will need batched access to anonymized outputs (can we allow cross-border pulls if data is tokenized/hashed?).

Questions we need clarified to recommend a concrete architecture
1) Data class: confirm whether the EU dataset contains PII as defined by your privacy team (yes/no).
2) QPS & concurrency: expected steady QPS and peak concurrency for the EU workload (estimate).
3) Cross-region reads: is cross-border access for aggregated reporting allowed if payloads are pseudonymized?
4) Compliance artifacts: standard ask — do you need SOC 2, encryption-at-rest keys in your KMS, and audit log export?

Our immediate recommendation options (high level)
- Private VPC (EU): Keeps EU data and model inference inside your VPC/region — best for strict residency and audit control.
- Hosted API (APAC): Use Redwood hosted endpoints in APAC for pilot traffic to avoid heavy ops.
- Dedicated reserve (US/internal): Reserved capacity for internal services that can tolerate US-hosted anonymized pulls, with routing rules.

Next steps
- Please confirm answers to the 4 qualification questions above (especially data class and QPS).
- I’ve attached a short MAP and a region availability matrix for reference.
- Proposal: schedule a 60-minute technical deep dive (Jonas + Evelyn) next week to walk infra options and KMS/SAML details.

Attachments: nova-map-initial-MAP.pdf (MAP), region-availability-matrix.csv

Best,
Ben

From: Luca Moretti <luca.moretti@novabanc.com>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 08:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Cross-border access & hosting model assessment — NovaBanc follow-up

Ben — thanks for the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

Answers to your qualification questions
1) Data class: Yes — EU transaction payloads contain PII (names, masked account numbers) per our privacy classification. Must remain in EU.
2) QPS/concurrency: For EU customers during steady-state expect ~40 qps with peaks up to 200 qps during batch windows. Initial pilot is smaller (~10 qps).
3) Cross-region reads: Aggregated reporting is allowed to leave the EU only if payloads are irreversibly pseudonymized (we use a SHA‑256 salt approach). Need to confirm with legal but that is our working assumption.
4) Compliance: SOC 2 is required for production, plus customer-managed KMS if we go Private VPC. Audit log retention of 12 months is mandatory.

Follow-ups / asks
- Can Redwood support a hybrid route where EU inference never leaves EU compute (Private VPC or EU Dedicated) and APAC traffic hits Redwood-hosted APAC endpoints?
- If we start with EU Private VPC, what is the typical lead time for provisioning an EU pilot (2–4 nodes)?
- We need a short doc on how cross-region routing/fallback would work operationally (e.g., what happens on EU capacity exhaustion).

We’re available for a technical review Tuesday or Wednesday next week (CEST).

— Luca
Luca Moretti
Head of Platform Integrations | NovaBanc
luca.moretti@novabanc.com | +44 20 7946 0123

Luca — perfect, thanks for the quick detail — that largely aligns with what we expected and lets us scope two immediate pilots:

Recommended approach (actionable)- Phase A (EU): Private VPC pilot hosted in an EU region to guarantee residency and support customer-managed KMS + 12m audit logs. We can run the pilot on a 2-node Dedicated cluster if you prefer Redwood-managed Dedicated inside a VPC; both are viable.
- Phase B (APAC): Redwood-hosted endpoints for APAC pilot to reduce time-to-value (we’ll route APAC traffic to APAC hosts; data there will be stored in APAC region).

Operational notes
- Cross-region routing: we’ll configure policy-based routing by source/customer. On EU capacity exhaustion we will failover to a pre-approved EU-compatible fallback (e.g., a warm Dedicated variant). We will not route EU-resident PII to APAC/US.
- Pseudonymization: We can accept hashed payloads for aggregated reporting transfers. Need final legal sign-off from your side.

Next steps (to get this started)
1) Technical deep dive: propose Tue 14 Sep 2027 10:00 CEST — Jonas (runtime) and Evelyn (security/compliance) will join.
2) Send proof-of-classification (one sample file / schema) and an example QPS trace if you have it; that speeds sizing.
3) We’ll prepare a short SOW for the EU pilot (incl timeline, seats, and estimated cost).

I attached a one-pager that sketches the hosting options so your legal/infra can skim it.

Attachments: hosting-options-onepager.pdf

Thanks — I’ll hold Tues 10:00 CEST for the deep-dive unless you prefer another slot.

Best,
Ben
